signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank International / Addiko Bank AG (Addiko Bank a.d. Beograd + Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd)
signals.signal: RBI WON the Addiko takeover contest. After the acceptance period expired on 29/07/2026 at 17:00 CEST, RBI announced acceptances for 10,831,435 Addiko shares = 56.16% of all shares subject to the offer, clearing its lowered 'more than 55%' minimum threshold (threshold cut announced 09-10/07/2026). Rival NLB's EUR 37.00/share bid lost to RBI's EUR 26.50/share. This REVERSES the baseline position (which had NLB at EUR37 vs RBI EUR26.50 and 50.42% acceptances at 09/06/2026). Consequence for Serbia: RBI now controls BOTH Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd and Addiko Bank a.d. Beograd, pointing to a Serbian entity merger and the consolidation of two ATM fleets, two POS/acquiring estates, two card portfolios and two core/channel stacks.
signals.source_name: RBI announcement via EQS News (Austrian Takeover Act publication) + Addiko Bank AG takeover-offer page
signals.implies: The single largest Serbian opportunity in this run. Bank mergers force: ATM fleet rationalisation and re-branding (NCR dispense/deposit/recycling + x-core multivendor software - Raiffeisen Serbia is ALREADY a Printec x-core reference customer, so the incumbent position can be extended over the Addiko estate), POS terminal and TMS consolidation, card re-issue and personalisation, HSM/key management and remote key injection re-keying, AML/KYC platform convergence, and heavy managed/field-services demand to physically touch every device.
signals.likelihood: Very high that integration planning starts in H2-2026; device/platform decisions typically land 6-18 months after closing, subject to NBS and competition approvals
signals.followup: FLAG TO ORCHESTRATOR AS PRIORITY. Immediately brief the Printec RS team to open an Addiko-integration conversation with Raiffeisen banka Srbija off the existing x-core relationship. Track: (a) official Austrian Takeover Act result publication, (b) NBS/competition-authority clearance, (c) settlement date, (d) any RBI statement on Serbian entity merger timing. Also count Addiko Serbia's ATM ('Addiko Express' multifunctional ATMs) and branch estate.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia + 18 Serbian commercial banks
signals.signal: SEPA Credit Transfer became OPERATIONAL in Serbia on 05/05/2026. The European Payments Council approved adherence applications from the NBS and 18 Serbian commercial banks; they were formally entered in the scheme participant register on 10/04/2026, and NBS announced the banking sector fully operational for SCT payments and collections with abroad from 05/05/2026. NBS states the NEXT phase is gradual bank adherence to SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst). This is a material advance on the baseline, which only recorded Serbia's admission to the SEPA geographical scope on 22/05/2025 with 'earliest operational readiness May 2026'. Plain language: SEPA = the single euro payments area; SCT is the standard euro credit transfer, SCT Inst is the ~10-second version; both run on ISO 20022 XML messaging.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia (SEPA release, nbs.rs id=20593) + NBS statement of 03-05/05/2026 reported by B92 / NIN / RTV
signals.implies: All 18 adhering banks now run ISO 20022 message flows, and the announced SCT Inst phase forces 24/7 instant rails with in-line sanctions/fraud screening and intraday liquidity monitoring. Direct fit for Printec instant-payments / ISO 20022 integration work, INETCO transaction monitoring, and IMTF Siron real-time screening. Banks NOT yet SCT Inst-adherent are the warm list.
signals.likelihood: High - SCT Inst adherence is stated NBS policy for the next phase; expect bank-by-bank projects through 2026-2027
signals.followup: Pull the EPC SCT / SCT Inst participant register to NAME the 18 Serbian adherents (only the aggregate count is confirmed so far - do not guess names). Then target non-SCT-Inst banks with an instant-payments readiness + screening offer.

signals.entity: AikBank a.d. Beograd, OTP banka Srbija a.d. Novi Sad, UniCredit Bank Srbija a.d.
signals.signal: Mastercard executed Serbia's FIRST live real-world 'agentic' payment transactions in June 2026 with three partner banks - AikBank, OTP banka Srbija and UniCredit Bank Srbija - using Mastercard Agent Pay. An AI agent completed a purchase on behalf of the banks' cardholders on Mastercard's Priceless.com platform, using agent-specific payment TOKENS for sensitive-data protection and strong identity verification with explicit cardholder consent. OTP banka Srbija carries this on its own newsroom dated 18/06/2026. Plain language: 'agentic payments' = an AI assistant pays on your behalf; the security model rests on tokenisation (a throwaway card number) plus identity/consent proof rather than the physical card.
signals.source_name: OTP banka Srbija newsroom (otpbanka.rs/alert) + Serbian press (BizLife, Biznis Kurir, Magazin Biznis, BIF)
signals.implies: Three Serbian banks are already live on agent tokenisation. That forces upgrades in card issuing/tokenisation, key management (Thales HSM, PCI-PIN, remote key injection), strong customer authentication/eIDAS-grade identity proofing, and real-time fraud monitoring of a brand-new non-human transaction class (INETCO). Also a credible entry hook: agentic transactions break conventional fraud rules.
signals.likelihood: High that these three banks expand agentic/tokenised commerce in the next 6-12 months; the fraud-monitoring gap is immediate
signals.followup: Get the Mastercard Serbia press release itself for the exact date and named banks (press coverage clusters 18-19/06/2026). Pitch INETCO + HSM/tokenisation hardening to all three, and note AikBank is already an NCR-recycler reference customer of Printec.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (Law on Interbank Fees)
signals.signal: NBS published a DRAFT of amendments to the 'Zakon o medjubankarskim naknadama i posebnim pravilima poslovanja kod platnih transakcija na osnovu platnih kartica' (Law on Interbank Fees and Special Rules for Card Payment Transactions), reported 16/06/2026, with the public consultation reported as running to 11/06/2026. For the first time it extends interchange caps to cards ISSUED ABROAD when used at Serbian points of sale or on Serbian e-commerce sites. Caps reported: domestic debit 0.20% / domestic credit 0.30%; foreign-issued cards online 1.15% debit / 1.50% credit. Stated purpose: align with EU practice, improve transparency and cut merchants' card-acceptance costs. Plain language: 'interchange' is the slice of every card payment that the merchant's bank pays the cardholder's bank - capping it squeezes acquiring revenue and pushes banks to compete on terminal capability and cost instead.
signals.source_name: Paragraf.rs daily legal news (item 170626-vest7) + Nova Ekonomija / N1 / Biznis Kurir / BIF coverage of the NBS draft
signals.implies: Compressed acquiring margins make POS estate TCO the deciding factor: banks respond by cutting terminal cost per merchant (softPOS instead of hardware), centralising estate control (TMS), and automating merchant onboarding (digital onboarding/eKYC). Squarely Printec POS/acquiring/TMS + softPOS + onboarding territory. Also creates card-system parametrisation work at every issuer.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that the amendments are adopted within 12 months given the consultation is closed
signals.followup: Retrieve the NBS draft text and the Sluzbeni glasnik publication once adopted, and confirm the exact consultation window (press dates 11/06 and 16/06/2026 are inconsistent - do not treat either as settled). Then build a 'post-interchange-cap acquiring economics' pitch for Serbian acquirers.
